m1.note: Raises bus-factor/adoption and lack of a third-party audit, but never claims cadence or team size leaves the code unreviewed.

m2.quote: Implementing an OAuth 2.1 authorization server from scratch is historically one of the easiest things to get subtly wrong (redirect URI validation, PKCE downgrade, token replay), and doing it as one module among a dozen inside a broader data-platform project is a yellow flag regardless of how carefully the README describes the mitigations.
m2.note: Treats the built-in authorization server as home-grown auth and a red flag.

m3.note: Engages the DOI benchmark directly and criticizes its independence/design, not its existence.

m4.note: Correctly notes only cross-enrichment needs DataHub and even says modularity mitigates lock-in.
